beats.text: Round of introductions. Your turn is next. What did the person before you just say?
In a classic experiment, people took turns reading words aloud. Afterwards, they barely remembered the words read just before their own turn.
While you rehearse your line, your brain stops recording.
Knowing about it helps. People told to focus on the speaker before them avoided the gap.
So next round: listen first. Then talk.

sources: Brenner (1973). The next-in-line effect. Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior 12. Words read in the ~9 s before one's own turn were recalled worse.
Bond (1985): encoding deficit; participants instructed to attend to the preceding events avoided the deficit. Via Wikipedia 'Next-in-line effect'.
